long_biography.plain_text:
Kenneth C. Griffin began investing as a Harvard freshman in 1986 and launched a small hedge fund from his dorm room the following year, using quantitative analysis to guide trades. After graduating, he founded Citadel in 1990. The investment firm became the principal source of his wealth and, despite devastating 2008 losses, grew into one of the most profitable hedge-fund managers by cumulative net gains.

Griffin and his partners established Citadel Securities in 2002 as options markets moved toward electronic trading. The separate market-making firm later became a major liquidity provider across global markets, while Griffin remained Citadel's founder, chief executive and co-chief investment officer. He has also channelled later public activity through Griffin Catalyst, supporting education, medical research and civic institutions.
